message:
[Page 1] How Fernwood runs Fernwood Labs is a 14-person software company in Chicago. We build data tools for mid-size healthcare and logistics companies. There are five teams: Leadership (Wade Wilson, founder), Engineering (led by Priya Nair), Growth (led by Dev Kumar), Operations (Krishna) and Finance (Lena Ortiz, part time). Until now we have run on Zoho and a lot of spreadsheets. The export attached has our people, candidates, software vendors, expenses, leave and customer contracts. This write-up says how each part works today; the policies say the rules. Everyone reports to one manager. Managers approve their team's time off. Wade and Krishna look after every customer contract; account managers look after their own. [Page 4] Customers We have 12 customer contracts. Each has an owner at Fernwood, a yearly value, a start date, a renewal date and a notice period. A contract starts as a draft, is signed, becomes active, and comes up for renewal; then it is renewed or ended. The owner is reminded 60 days before the notice date, and the contract moves to renewal due. When a contract comes up for renewal, a request starts in Spend for the budget owner, so the renewal is budgeted. Some contracts have a customer contact at the customer; they are not Fernwood people. Questions about this write-up go to Krishna. [Page 15] Customer contracts Every contract has an owner at Fernwood, a yearly value, a start date, a renewal date and a notice period in days. The notice date is the renewal date less the notice period. Sixty days before the notice date, the contract moves to renewal due and its owner is asked to act. If nobody has acted 30 days before the notice date, Wade and the owner are told. [Page 16] Customer contracts (continued) Contracts over $50,000 a year go through legal review before they are signed. When a contract comes up for renewal, a renewal request starts in Spend for the budget owner. Wade and Krishna see every contract; owners see their own. Tables attached (name, header and row count; the cells are data too): "Customer","Annual Value","Start Date","Renewal Date","Notice Days","Account Owner","Billing Email","Customer Contact","Status"
Latest message from Wade Wilson: Set up Customer contracts: Contracts, renewals and notice dates. Each contract has an owner at Fernwood, a yearly value, start and renewal dates and a notice period. It moves from draft to signed, active, renewal due, then renewed or ended. Owners are reminded ahead of the notice date, and a renewal starts a request in Spend. Wade and Krishna see every contract and owners see their own. Its rules, from the policies: - The notice date is the renewal date less the notice period. - 60 days before the notice date, the contract moves to renewal due and its owner is asked to act. - If nobody has acted 30 days before the notice date, Wade and the owner are told. - A contract over $50,000 a year goes through legal review before it is signed. - When a contract comes up for renewal, a renewal request starts in Spend for the budget owner. Where it connects to what is already built: - a contract up for renewal starts a request in Spend Its rows come from contracts.csv, imported into its first sheet. The file's columns fill plain columns of that sheet (text, dates, amounts, people, choices, steps); a link can't be filled from a file, so a link column there stays empty for imported rows.
